decisions.choice: the word that came to Jeremiah: a heading that opens a new message
decisions.reason: The same heading opens the temple sermon (7:1) and the covenant sermon (11:1). What follows is a prose account of an acted lesson at a potter's workshop and the message drawn from it (verses 2-12). Poetry follows in verses 13-17, and verses 18-23 tell of a plot against Jeremiah and his prayer about it.

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying: / This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD: / This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah:
decisions.reason: The book's fixed wording for this heading (as in 7:1 and 11:1). Balanced puts it as a plain statement and drops "saying", which only introduces the quotation; Readable says it more simply still.

decisions.choice: La palabra que vino a Jeremías de parte del SEÑOR, diciendo: / Este mensaje vino a Jeremías de parte del SEÑOR: / Este es el mensaje que el SEÑOR le dio a Jeremías:
alternatives: La palabra que vino a Jeremías del SEÑOR
decisions.reason: The fixed Spanish wording of this heading in Jeremiah, used for the whole block. Literal keeps "diciendo", which only introduces the quotation; Balanced drops it, and Readable says who gave the message.

decisions.choice: Neno lililomjia Yeremia kutoka kwa BWANA, kusema: / Ujumbe huu ulimjia Yeremia kutoka kwa BWANA: / Huu ndio ujumbe ambao BWANA alimpa Yeremia:
decisions.reason: The fixed Swahili wording of this heading in Jeremiah at each level; Literal keeps "kusema" for the Hebrew "saying", Balanced and Readable drop it as the English does.

decisions.choice: "La parole qui fut adressée à Jérémie de la part du SEIGNEUR, disant :" (L); "Ce message fut adressé à Jérémie par le SEIGNEUR :" (B); "Voici le message que le SEIGNEUR a donné à Jérémie :" (R)
alternatives: La parole qui vint à Jérémie
decisions.reason: The fixed French wording of Jeremiah's heading for Jeremiah 18-34, built on Kings' "fut adressée à X". Balanced drops "disant", which only opens the quotation, as the English drops "saying".

decisions.choice: First-person narrative (Jeremiah 18-20): passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("je descendis"), passé composé at Readable ("je suis descendu"); the LORD's words and the oracles stay in the tenses of speech
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for Jeremiah's own narrative, like Revelation: the written narrative tense at L and B, the spoken one at R. Speech never takes the passé simple.

decisions.choice: "Lời từ CHÚA đến với Giê-rê-mi rằng:" / "Sứ điệp này từ CHÚA đến với Giê-rê-mi:" / "Đây là sứ điệp CHÚA ban cho Giê-rê-mi:"
alternatives: "Có lời của CHÚA phán cùng Giê-rê-mi"
decisions.reason: The heading formula settled for Jeremiah in the terms note, kept the same at each level through chapters 18-34. "Sứ điệp" (message) at Balanced and Readable matches the English; Literal keeps "lời" (word) and "rằng" for "saying".

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 예레미야에게 임한 말씀" (L); "이것은 ... 주신 말씀이다" (B); "... 주신 말씀은 이러하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's fixed wording for this heading in Jeremiah. The narrator speaks of God, so the verbs take the honorific; "saying" is carried by the colon-like close of the heading rather than by a separate verb.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}" for the divine name, with the particle outside the span
decisions.reason: The Korean style guide's span for YHWH throughout Jeremiah: "주" by default, "야훼" with the setting. Both end in a vowel, so one particle (께서, 가, 의, 를) fits both. Korean has no capital letters, so the English deity_pronoun spans have no Korean counterpart; respect for God is carried by "-시-" and "께서".

decisions.choice: "ከእግዚአብሔር ወደ ኤርምያስ የመጣው ቃል ይህ ነው" (L), "ይህ መልእክት ከእግዚአብሔር ወደ ኤርምያስ መጣ" (B), "እግዚአብሔር ለኤርምያስ የሰጠው መልእክት ይህ ነው" (R)
decisions.reason: The heading formula of Jeremiah, worded to sit beside "የእግዚአብሔር ቃል ወደ እኔ መጣ".

decisions.choice: वह वचन जो {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की ओर से यिर्मयाह के पास पहुँचा (L); ... यह संदेश पहुँचा (B); {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने यिर्मयाह को यह संदेश दिया (R)
decisions.reason: The heading "the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD", worded to match the prophets note's formula "the word of the LORD came to X" at each level (वचन ... पहुँचा; संदेश दिया at Readable), the same each time it returns (21:1).

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Hindi
decisions.reason: The English marks God's pronouns with the deity_pronoun setting. Devanagari has no capital letters, so the Hindi has no such spans; respect for God comes from the honorific third person, and Jeremiah's prayer (verses 19-23) addresses God with तू. This holds for the whole file.

decisions.choice: Слово, которое было к Иеремии от ГОСПОДА, говоря: (L); Вот слово, с которым ГОСПОДЬ обратился к Иеремии: (B); Вот слово, которое ГОСПОДЬ дал Иеремии: (R)
alternatives: Слово, которое было к Иеремии от ГОСПОДА (every level)
decisions.reason: The heading formula of Jeremiah, worded to match the "word of the LORD came" formula the prophets note sets: "было ... к" at Literal, "обратился к" at Balanced, "дал ... слово" at Readable.

decisions.choice: the potter's house: the workshop where a potter shaped and fired clay pots
decisions.reason: Clay jars, bowls and lamps were the everyday containers of the ancient world, and potters worked near a supply of clay and water. Jeremiah "goes down" to the workshop, which suggests it lay below the temple and the upper city, perhaps near the Potsherd Gate that led out to the valley of Ben-hinnom (19:2).

decisions.choice: arise and go down: a call to set out at once
decisions.reason: "Arise" before another verb of motion urges the hearer to start doing it (13:4, 6). It does not mean that Jeremiah was lying or sitting down.

decisions.choice: there I will let you hear my words: the message will come at the workshop, through what Jeremiah sees
decisions.reason: God does not give the word first and then send Jeremiah to act it out. The lesson is given at the potter's house, after Jeremiah has watched the potter at work (verses 5-6).

decisions.choice: the potter's workshop
decisions.reason: "House" here is a place of work. Readable says "workshop" so that young readers do not picture the potter's home.

decisions.choice: la casa del alfarero (Literal, Balanced); el taller del alfarero (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for the potter's workshop. Readable says "taller" so that the reader does not picture the potter's home, as the English Readable says "workshop".

decisions.choice: quotation marks « » for the LORD's words to Jeremiah
decisions.reason: In this prose account the LORD's words to Jeremiah are quoted as prose speech, as the English does; the message he is to pass on (verse 11) takes “ ” inside them.

decisions.choice: karakana ya mfinyanzi
decisions.reason: "House" here is a place of work, so Readable says "karakana" (workshop), as the English Readable says "workshop".

decisions.choice: "l'atelier du potier" (R); "la maison du potier" (L, B)
alternatives: la maison du potier at every level
decisions.reason: As the terms note and the English: Readable says "workshop" so that readers do not picture the potter's home.

decisions.choice: God says "Ta" for himself and "ngươi" (Literal) / "con" (Balanced, Readable) to Jeremiah
decisions.reason: The address settled for the book in the terms note: God speaking says "Ta", and to the prophet "ngươi" at Literal and "con" at Balanced and Readable, as he speaks to Hezekiah in 2 Kings 19:20 and 20:5. "Ta" takes the deity_pronoun span in mid-sentence and is written plainly at the start of a sentence or line.

decisions.choice: "thợ gốm" (potter); "xưởng" (workshop) at Readable
decisions.reason: "Thợ gốm" is the potter of Romans 9:21, kept through the chapter so that the picture of verses 4-6 and 11 is heard each time.

decisions.choice: "토기장이의 집" (L, B); "그릇 만드는 사람의 작업장" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's forms for the potter in Jeremiah, as Matthew 27:7 (토기장이). Readable says what he does in plain words and calls his "house" a workshop, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: God speaks to Jeremiah in 해라체 ("내려가거라", "들려주겠다")
decisions.reason: As the terms note: God speaks in the plain style with 나 and 너, and his speech in this prose account takes quotation marks, as the English does.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Amharic.

decisions.choice: "ሸክላ ሠሪ" for the potter; "ጭቃ" for the clay
decisions.reason: The words of the Amharic Romans 9:21, which takes up this picture (the potter's right over the clay); the pot is "ዕቃ" (L) and "ማሰሮ" (B, R) as there.

decisions.choice: कुम्हार का कारख़ाना (R)
decisions.reason: "House" here is a workshop (meaning m1); Readable says so, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: мастерская
decisions.reason: "House" here is the potter's place of work; Readable says "мастерская", as the English says "workshop".

sw.R: Basi nilishuka mpaka karakana ya mfinyanzi. Nikamwona huko akifanya kazi kwenye gurudumu lake la kufinyangia.

vi.L: Vậy tôi đi xuống nhà người thợ gốm, và kìa, ông ấy đang làm việc trên bàn xoay.
vi.B: Vậy tôi đi xuống nhà người thợ gốm, và thấy ông đang làm việc bên bàn xoay.

ko.L: 그래서 내가 토기장이의 집으로 내려갔는데, 보아라, 그가 물레 위에서 일을 하고 [있었다].
ko.B: 그래서 내가 토기장이의 집으로 내려가 보니, 그가 물레를 돌리며 일하고 있었다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 그릇 만드는 사람의 작업장으로 내려갔다. 그는 거기에서 물레를 돌리며 일하고 있었다.

pt.B: Então desci à casa do oleiro, e lá estava ele, trabalhando no torno.
pt.R: Então desci até a oficina do oleiro. Eu o vi lá, trabalhando no seu torno de oleiro.

am.L: ወደ ሸክላ ሠሪውም ቤት ወረድኩ፤ እነሆም፣ እርሱ በመንኮራኩሩ ላይ ሥራ ይሠራ [ነበር]።

hi.L: तब मैं कुम्हार के घर उतर गया, और देखो, वह चाक पर काम कर [रहा था]।

decisions.choice: the two stones: the potter's wheel, made of two discs
decisions.reason: The word means "a pair of stones". A potter's wheel had two discs joined by an upright shaft: the potter turned the lower one with his feet and shaped the clay on the upper one. The same word names the stones a woman sat on to give birth (Exodus 1:16), which were also a pair.

decisions.choice: look, he was doing work: the scene as Jeremiah came upon it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word that draws attention puts the reader beside Jeremiah as he arrives and sees the potter already busy (as in 13:7). The written text joins the pronoun to that word; the text as read keeps them separate. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the wheel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "two stones" is one object, so every level says "wheel"; the literal form is given in meaning decision m1.

decisions.choice: look (Literal); there he was (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps a word that calls attention, as in 13:7. Balanced uses an English turn of phrase with the same effect, and Readable says "I saw".

decisions.choice: la rueda (Literal); el torno (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "two stones" is the potter's wheel, made of two discs. Literal says "la rueda", as the English says "the wheel"; Balanced and Readable use "torno", the ordinary Spanish word for a potter's wheel.

decisions.choice: gurudumu
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "two stones" is the potter's wheel, so every level says "gurudumu"; Readable adds "la kufinyangia" (for shaping clay).

decisions.choice: "le tour" (the potter's wheel)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "two stones" is one object, the potter's wheel; French names it with its own word, "le tour" (a potter's "tour"), as the English says "wheel". "La roue" would suggest a cart wheel.

decisions.choice: "bàn xoay" (wheel)
decisions.reason: As in the English, every level names the one object, the potter's wheel; the literal "two stones" is given in meaning decision m1. Jeremiah narrates as "tôi" and calls the potter "ông".

decisions.choice: "물레" for the "two stones"
decisions.reason: As the English, every level names the object, the potter's wheel; "물레" is the everyday Korean word for it. The literal "two stones" is explained in meaning decision m1.

decisions.choice: o torno (L, B); o torno de oleiro (R)
decisions.reason: The "two stones" are the potter's wheel (m1), which Brazilian Portuguese calls "o torno" (de oleiro); "a roda" is less clear. Like the English, every level names the one object, and the meaning note gives the Hebrew picture.

decisions.choice: चाक
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "two stones" is the potter's wheel (meaning m1); Hindi has the exact everyday word, चाक, at every level.

decisions.choice: на кругу (L); за гончарным кругом (B, R)
decisions.reason: The "two stones" are the potter's wheel, made of two discs (the meaning decision); every level names the wheel, as the English does.

en.L: And the vessel that he was making of clay was spoiled in the potter's hand, and he made it again into another vessel, as it was right in the eyes of the potter to do.
en.B: If the pot he was shaping from the clay went wrong in the potter's hand, he would make it over into another pot, whatever seemed best to him.
en.R: Sometimes the pot he was shaping from the clay did not turn out well in his hands. Then he would shape the clay into another pot, in whatever way he thought best.

decisions.choice: was spoiled ... and he made it again: what the potter did whenever a pot went wrong
decisions.reason: The verb forms can describe something that happened again and again. Jeremiah watched the potter at work, and the lesson in verse 6 is about what a potter is able to do, so the verse is best read as his usual practice. It could also tell of one pot that Jeremiah saw spoiled and reshaped; the lesson is the same.

decisions.choice: spoiled: ruined, no longer fit for its purpose
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the ruined loincloth (13:7, 9). Here the ruin is not final: the potter still has the clay in his hand and can make something new from it.

decisions.choice: as was right in the eyes of the potter: as the potter himself judged best
decisions.reason: "Right in someone's eyes" means what seems good to that person. The new pot is made to the potter's own design, not to the clay's. The phrase prepares for the question of verse 6.

decisions.choice: pot
decisions.reason: The word means any vessel or container. Since this one is made of clay on a potter's wheel, Balanced and Readable say "pot"; Literal keeps "vessel".

decisions.choice: If ... / Sometimes ... Then ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the repeated action described in meaning decision m1 with "if ... would" and "sometimes ... then".

decisions.choice: Si ... se le estropeaba ... hacía (Balanced); A veces ... Entonces ... volvía a moldear (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the Spanish imperfect to show the potter's usual practice (meaning decision m1), as the English uses "would" and "sometimes". Literal keeps the preterite of a single event.

decisions.choice: chungu
decisions.reason: The vessel is a clay pot made on the wheel, so Balanced and Readable say "chungu"; Literal keeps the general "chombo".

decisions.choice: imparfait "se gâtait ... refaisait" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable read the verse as the potter's usual practice (meaning decision m1), which French says with the imparfait of repeated action; Literal keeps the passé simple of a single event, as the Hebrew narrative form reads.

decisions.choice: "망가지면 ... 만들었다" (L); "잘못되면 ... 빚었다" (B); "... 때가 있었다. 그러면" (R)
decisions.reason: The verbs describe what the potter did whenever a pot went wrong (meaning decision m1), so Korean uses "-면" and, at Readable, "때가 있었다", the Korean way of showing a repeated action.

decisions.choice: a argila; o vaso; se estragou (L), se estragava (B)
decisions.reason: "Argila" is the potter's word for his clay, and "vaso" covers any pot he makes; both return in verse 6. The verb is the one used of the ruined loincloth (m2), so Literal and Balanced repeat "estragar" from 13:7 and 13:9.

decisions.choice: जब कभी ... बिगड़ जाता, तो ... बना लेता (B); कभी-कभी ... तब ... बना देता (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the potter's repeated action (meaning m1) with Hindi habitual forms; Literal keeps the Hebrew's simple past.

decisions.choice: nishchat "損なわれる" (L), "うまくいかない" (B, R) (m2); keli "器" (L, B), "つぼ" (R); chomer "粘土"; B and R make the repeated action explicit ("〜のだった" / "そういうとき"), as the English B, R (m1, uncertain).
decisions.reason: As the English levels.

records.literal_gloss: Like the potter this not can I do to you, house of Israel? declares Yahweh. Behold, like the clay in [the] hand of the potter, so you [are] in my hand, house of Israel.

en.L: "Can I not do with you as this potter [does], house of Israel? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Look, like the clay in the potter's hand, so [are] you in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, house of Israel.
en.B: "House of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. As the clay is in the potter's hand, so you are in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, house of Israel.
en.R: "People of Israel, can I not do with you what this potter does? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You are in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands just as the clay is in the potter's hands.

es.L: «¿No podré yo hacer {{plural_you:con ustedes|con vosotros}} como este alfarero, casa de Israel?, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. He aquí, como el barro en la mano del alfarero, así {{plural_you:son ustedes|sois vosotros}} en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano, casa de Israel.
es.B: «Casa de Israel, ¿acaso no puedo yo hacer {{plural_you:con ustedes|con vosotros}} lo mismo que hace este alfarero?, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Como el barro está en la mano del alfarero, así {{plural_you:están ustedes|estáis vosotros}} en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano, casa de Israel.
es.R: «Pueblo de Israel, ¿acaso no puedo hacer {{plural_you:con ustedes|con vosotros}} lo que hace este alfarero?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. {{plural_you:Ustedes están|Vosotros estáis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} manos igual que el barro está en las manos del alfarero.

fr.L: « Ne puis-je pas faire de vous comme ce potier, maison d’Israël ? déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Voici, comme l’argile dans la main du potier, ainsi [êtes-]vous dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main, maison d’Israël.
fr.B: « Maison d’Israël, ne puis-je pas agir avec vous comme ce potier ? déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Comme l’argile est dans la main du potier, ainsi vous êtes dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main, maison d’Israël.
fr.R: « Peuple d’Israël, est-ce que je ne peux pas faire avec vous ce que fait ce potier ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Vous êtes dans {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} mains comme l’argile est dans les mains du potier.

sw.L: "Je, siwezi kuwafanyia ninyi kama mfinyanzi huyu [afanyavyo], nyumba ya Israeli? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Tazama, kama udongo mkononi mwa mfinyanzi, ndivyo [mlivyo] ninyi mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}}, nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.B: "Nyumba ya Israeli, je, siwezi kuwatendea kama mfinyanzi huyu anavyofanya? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Kama udongo ulivyo mkononi mwa mfinyanzi, ndivyo mlivyo ninyi mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}}, nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.R: "Watu wa Israeli, je, siwezi kuwafanyia kama mfinyanzi huyu anavyofanya? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ninyi mko mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}} kama udongo ulivyo mikononi mwa mfinyanzi.

vi.L: "Hỡi nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên, chẳng lẽ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không thể làm cho các ngươi như người thợ gốm này [làm] sao? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy. Kìa, như đất sét trong tay người thợ gốm thể nào, thì các ngươi ở trong tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thể ấy, hỡi nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: "Hỡi nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên, chẳng lẽ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không thể làm với các ngươi như người thợ gốm này đã làm sao? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy. Đất sét ở trong tay người thợ gốm thế nào, thì các ngươi ở trong tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng thế ấy, hỡi nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: "Hỡi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, chẳng lẽ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không thể làm với các ngươi như người thợ gốm này đã làm sao? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Các ngươi ở trong tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} giống như đất sét ở trong tay người thợ gốm.

ko.L: "이스라엘 집아, 이 토기장이처럼 내가 너희에게 할 수 없겠느냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 보아라, 토기장이의 손에 있는 진흙처럼, 이스라엘 집아, 너희가 내 손에 [있다].
ko.B: "이스라엘 집아, 이 토기장이가 하는 것처럼 내가 너희에게 할 수 없겠느냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 진흙이 토기장이의 손에 있듯이, 이스라엘 집아, 너희는 내 손에 있다.
ko.R: "이스라엘 백성아, 이 사람이 진흙으로 하는 것처럼 내가 너희에게 할 수 없겠느냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 진흙이 그릇 만드는 사람의 손에 있듯이 너희는 내 손에 있다.

pt.L: "Não posso eu fazer com vocês como este oleiro, casa de Israel? declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Eis que, tal como a argila na mão do oleiro, assim [estão] vocês na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão, casa de Israel.
pt.B: "Casa de Israel, será que não posso fazer com vocês o que este oleiro faz? declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Vocês estão na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão do mesmo modo que a argila está na mão do oleiro, casa de Israel.
pt.R: "Povo de Israel, será que eu não posso fazer com vocês o que este oleiro faz? diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Vocês estão nas {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} mãos, assim como a argila está nas mãos do oleiro.

decisions.choice: can I not do: a question that expects the answer "yes, you can"
decisions.reason: The question is a strong way of saying that God has the same power over Israel that the potter has over his clay. The comparison is with the potter's action, not with his skill: what he does with a spoiled pot (verse 4).

decisions.choice: like the clay in the potter's hand: Israel's future is in God's hands, and he is free to reshape it
decisions.reason: The picture is of God's rule over his people. Verses 7-10 show that this freedom is not whim: God reshapes a nation in answer to how it turns, toward evil or away from it. The picture can be read both as a warning (the people can be reworked) and as hope (spoiled clay is not thrown away).

decisions.choice: the potter and the clay: a picture Isaiah also uses
decisions.reason: Isaiah speaks of the clay that cannot question the potter (Isaiah 29:16; 45:9) and of God as the potter and his people as the clay (Isaiah 64:7). Paul draws on the picture when he writes of God's freedom in Romans 9:20-21.

decisions.choice: People of Israel
decisions.reason: "House of Israel" means the people descended from Israel. Readable says "people" and names them once.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD in the middle of the question
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the formula after the question and before the picture of the clay; every level keeps it there, as Isaiah's wording does.

decisions.choice: declara el SEÑOR (Literal); afirma el SEÑOR (Balanced); dice el SEÑOR (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Spanish wording of neʾum YHWH for the whole block, always after a comma. Here it stands after the question, as in the Hebrew, so the question mark comes before the comma.

decisions.choice: plural you: {{plural_you:con ustedes|con vosotros}}
decisions.reason: Every plural "you" in the block is a plural_you span, Latin American "ustedes" by default with "vosotros" as the alternative, covering the pronoun or verb that changes. Here God speaks to the whole house of Israel.

decisions.choice: asema BWANA (Literal, Balanced); anasema BWANA (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili wording of the formula "declares the LORD" (2 Kings 19:33), kept in the middle of the question where the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: "déclare le SEIGNEUR" (L, B); "dit le SEIGNEUR" (R)
alternatives: dit le SEIGNEUR at every level
decisions.reason: The fixed French wording of neʾum YHWH for Jeremiah 18-34, as 2 Kings 19:33 and 22:19.

decisions.choice: to uproot and to tear down and to destroy: the words of Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: These are three of the four words of judgment in 1:10, where God set Jeremiah over nations and kingdoms. Verse 9 takes up the two words of restoration. Here God explains how that call works: the word he speaks over a nation is not the last word, because the nation's response matters (verses 8 and 10).

decisions.choice: at one moment: at any time
decisions.reason: The word means an instant. With its partner in verse 9 it means "at one time ... at another time": whenever God speaks a word of judgment or of blessing.

decisions.choice: a nation or a kingdom: any nation, not only Israel
decisions.reason: The rule is stated for all peoples, as in 1:10, before it is applied to Judah in verse 11. Jonah 3 shows it at work for Nineveh.

decisions.choice: uproot, tear down, destroy
decisions.reason: The same English verbs as in 1:10 at every level, so the reader hears the echo.

decisions.choice: may speak / may announce
decisions.reason: The verb describes something that can happen at any time, so English adds "may". Literal and Balanced end with a comma because the sentence runs on into verse 8; Readable ends the sentence here.

decisions.choice: arrancar, derribar, destruir
decisions.reason: The same Spanish verbs at every level each time the words of Jeremiah's call (1:10) return, so the reader hears the echo; verse 9 adds "edificar" and "plantar".

decisions.choice: kung'oa, kubomoa, kuangamiza
decisions.reason: The same Swahili verbs as Jeremiah's call (1:10) at every level, so the reader hears the echo; verse 9 adds "kujenga" and "kupanda".

decisions.choice: "arracher, démolir, détruire" (and "bâtir, planter" in verse 9)
decisions.reason: The same French verbs each time Jeremiah's call (1:10) returns (24:6; 31:28), so the echo is heard as in the English.

decisions.choice: "nhổ đi, phá đổ ... hủy diệt"
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah's call (1:10), kept the same each time they return in these chapters (verse 9; 24:6; 31:28) so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: "뽑고 허물고 멸하다"
decisions.reason: The same Korean verbs at each return of the words of Jeremiah's call (1:10; 18:7-9; 24:6; 31:28; 42:10; 45:4), at every level, so the echo can be heard.

decisions.choice: Each verse closed as its own sentence at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: A conditional Korean sentence would have to put the main clause of verse 8 before the verse marker; Balanced and Readable make verse 7 a sentence of its own ("말할 수 있다"), and Literal keeps the run-on with "-더라도".

decisions.choice: arrancar, derrubar, destruir (verse 7); construir, plantar (verse 9)
decisions.reason: The five verbs are those of Jeremiah's call (m1), and every level keeps the words 1:10 sets for them, so that the reader hears how that call works.

decisions.choice: "መንቀል፣ ማፍረስና ማጥፋት"; in verse 9 "መሥራትና መትከል"
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah's call in the Amharic of 1:10.

decisions.choice: उखाड़ना, ढा देना, नष्ट करना; बनाना, रोपना (verse 9)
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah's call (1:10), which return here and in 24:6, 31:28, 42:10 and 45:4. This block uses one Hindi verb for each; the drafts of 1:10 and the later chapters should use the same.

decisions.choice: जाति (L, B); देश (R)
decisions.reason: Goy here is any nation (meaning m3). जाति at Literal and Balanced as "nation", since it stands beside राज्य and the sense is clear; Readable says देश, as the poetry note keeps जाति out of the plainest level.

decisions.choice: вырвать с корнем, разрушить, погубить
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah's call (1:10), the same Russian verbs at every level wherever they return (18:7-9; 24:6; 31:28; 42:10; 45:4), so that the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: The call verbs of 1:10 (m1): lintosh "引き抜く", lintots "取り壊す", leha'avid "滅ぼす", the same at every level; 18:9 has the other two ("建てる", "植える").
decisions.reason: JEREMIAH CONVENTIONS: the six verbs of the call.

decisions.choice: I will relent: God turns from the judgment he announced when the nation turns from its evil
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used when God relented after Moses pleaded for Israel (Exodus 32:14), where its sense is explained. It does not mean that God was wrong or that he changes as people do (Numbers 23:19; 1 Samuel 15:29). These verses show that God's warnings are meant to bring people back: when a nation turns, God turns too. Jonah 3:10 tells of exactly this, and Jeremiah 26:3 and 26:13 apply it to Judah.

decisions.choice: its evil ... the evil that I planned: wrongdoing and the disaster that answers it
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew word stands for both. The nation's evil is its wickedness; the evil God plans is the harm or disaster of judgment. The repetition shows the one answering the other.

decisions.choice: against which I have spoken: the nation, not its evil, is what God spoke about
decisions.reason: The words "which I spoke against it" refer back to the nation of verse 7, over which God has spoken words of judgment.

decisions.choice: planned: devised, intended
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a craftsman's designs as well as of plans. It returns in verse 11, where God says he is devising a plan against Judah, and in verse 18, where the people make plans against Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: relent (Literal, Balanced); change my mind (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 32:14. "Repent" is avoided at every level, since in English it suggests turning from sin.

decisions.choice: disaster
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "evil" twice, as the Hebrew does. Balanced and Readable say "disaster" for the second, so that God is not heard planning wickedness (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: me retractaré (Literal); desistiré (Balanced); cambiaré de parecer (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb of God relenting (nicham). It is never "arrepentirse" here, which in Spanish suggests turning from sin (meaning decision m1; 1 Samuel 15 as published). Literal says "retractarse", as in 4:28 and 15:6; Balanced and Readable say he holds back or changes his mind.

decisions.choice: el desastre
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mal" for both Hebrew words, as the Hebrew does; Balanced and Readable say "desastre" for the harm God planned (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: nitaghairi (Literal, Balanced); nitabadili nia yangu (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Kughairi" is to call off what one intended; "kutubu" is avoided because it means repenting of sin.

decisions.choice: "je renoncerai" (L, B); "je changerai d'avis" (R)
decisions.reason: As Exodus 32:14 in French. "Se repentir" is avoided because it suggests turning from sin.

decisions.choice: "le malheur" for the second "evil" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English "disaster": Literal keeps "mal" twice as the Hebrew does; Balanced and Readable say "malheur" so that God is not heard planning wickedness.

decisions.choice: "đổi ý" (relent); "điều ác" for the nation's evil and "tai họa" for the evil God planned
decisions.reason: "Ăn năn" and "hối hận" suggest regret for sin and are avoided for God, as the English avoids "repent". Vietnamese cannot keep one word for both kinds of evil without making God plan wickedness, so even Literal says "tai họa" for the second, as meaning decision m2 explains.

decisions.choice: "뜻을 돌이키다" (L, B); "마음을 바꾸다" (R)
decisions.reason: God relents from the judgment he announced (meaning decision m1). "후회하다" would suggest regret over a mistake and "회개하다" turning from sin, so Korean says that he turns his purpose.

decisions.choice: "악" for the nation's evil; "재앙" for the evil God planned
decisions.reason: Korean has no one word for both wickedness and disaster (meaning decision m2); Literal keeps "악" for the nation and uses "재앙" for the harm God planned, so God is not heard planning wickedness.

decisions.choice: desistirei do mal (L), desistirei da desgraça (B); vou mudar de ideia (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is God turning back from a judgment he announced (m1). Literal and Balanced say "desistir de", as 4:28 sets it for the book, since "arrepender-se" would suggest that God had done wrong; Readable says "mudar de ideia", as 4:28 does. Literal keeps "o mal" twice, for the nation's evil and God's judgment (m2), as 11:11 sets it; Balanced and Readable say "desgraça" for the second. Verse 10 follows.

decisions.choice: "እጸጸታለሁ" (L), "… እመለሳለሁ" (B), "ሐሳቤን እለውጣለሁ" (R) for "I will relent"
decisions.reason: The levels follow the Amharic Exodus 32:14 (ተጸጸተ / ተመለሰ / ሐሳቡን ለወጠ).

decisions.choice: पछताऊँगा (L); रुक जाऊँगा (B); अपना मन बदल लूँगा (R)
decisions.reason: God relenting: the three wordings of Exodus 32:12-14 in this translation. मन फिराना is avoided, since the New Testament uses it for repenting of sin.

decisions.choice: विपत्ति (B, R) for the second "evil"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps बुराई twice, as the Hebrew does; Balanced and Readable say विपत्ति for the second, so that God is not heard planning wickedness (meaning m2).

decisions.choice: отменю (L); откажусь от (B); изменю моё решение (R)
decisions.reason: The verb nicham as in Exodus 32:14 in this translation; "раскаяться" is avoided because it suggests turning from sin.

decisions.choice: shav mera'ato "その悪から立ち帰る" (L, B), "悪を行うのをやめる" (R); nichamti "思い直す" (L, B), "考えを変え" (R); ra'ah as wrongdoing "悪" and as disaster "災い" (m2), the two senses of one Hebrew word.
decisions.reason: JER tables (shuv, ra'ah).

ru.B: А в другой раз {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} могу объявить о каком-то народе или царстве, что построю его и насажу,

uk.L: А іншої миті {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} можу сказати про народ чи про царство, щоб будувати і садити [його],

decisions.choice: to build and to plant: the two words of restoration in 1:10
decisions.reason: After the words of judgment in verse 7, these are the last two words of Jeremiah's call (1:10). They return as promises in 24:6 and 31:28.

decisions.choice: another
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "a moment". English says "at another moment" or "at another time" to show the contrast with verse 7.

decisions.choice: build up
decisions.reason: The same verb "build" as in 1:10. Readable adds "up", which English uses when a nation is made strong.

decisions.choice: otro momento / Otras veces
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "a moment"; Spanish says "en otro momento" to show the contrast with verse 7.

decisions.choice: "à un [autre] moment"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "at a moment"; French adds "autre" to mark the contrast with verse 7, in brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: livnot velintoa' "建て、植える" (L, B), "建て上げ、植える" (R), the restoration verbs of 1:10 (m1).
decisions.reason: JEREMIAH CONVENTIONS: the six verbs of the call.

records.literal_gloss: and it does the evil in my eyes, not listening to my voice, and I will relent concerning the good that I said to do good [to] it.

en.L: and it does the evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes, not listening to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice, then I will relent concerning the good that I said I would do for it.
en.B: but it does what is evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight and does not obey {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, then I will relent and not do the good I had promised it.
en.R: But if that nation does what I say is evil and does not obey {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will change {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind. I will not do the good things I had promised for it.

es.L: y hace lo malo ante {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos, no escuchando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz, entonces me retractaré del bien que dije que le haría.
es.B: pero si hace lo malo ante {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos y no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} obedece, entonces desistiré y no le haré el bien que le había prometido.
es.R: Pero si esa nación hace lo que yo considero malo y no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} obedece, cambiaré de parecer. No le daré las cosas buenas que le había prometido.

fr.L: et qu’elle fait ce qui est mal à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux, n’écoutant pas {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix, alors je renoncerai au bien que j’avais dit lui faire.
fr.B: mais si elle fait ce qui est mal à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux et ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}obéit pas, je renoncerai au bien que je lui avais promis.
fr.R: Mais si cette nation fait ce que je considère comme mal et ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}obéit pas, je changerai d’avis. Je ne lui ferai pas le bien que je lui avais promis.

vi.L: mà nó lại làm điều ác trước mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, không nghe tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đổi ý về điều tốt mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã phán sẽ làm cho nó.

vi.R: Nhưng nếu dân tộc ấy làm điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} coi là ác và không vâng lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đổi ý. Ta sẽ không làm những điều tốt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã hứa cho nó.

ko.L: 그것이 내 눈에 악한 일을 하고 내 목소리를 듣지 않으면, 나는 그것에게 선을 베풀겠다고 말한 그 선에 대하여 뜻을 돌이킨다.

pt.L: e, se ela fizer o mal aos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} olhos, não ouvindo a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} voz, então desistirei do bem que disse que lhe faria.

ja.R: しかし、もしその国が、わたしが悪いと言うことをし、わたしに従わないなら、わたしは考えを変え、その国に約束していた良いことをしない。

uk.L: а він чинитиме зло в {{deity_pronoun:моїх|Моїх}} очах, не слухаючи {{deity_pronoun:мого|Мого}} голосу, — тоді {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} пожалкую про те добро, яке сказав зробити йому.
uk.B: але він чинитиме зло в {{deity_pronoun:моїх|Моїх}} очах і не слухатиметься {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}}, — тоді {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} передумаю і не зроблю добра, яке обіцяв йому.
uk.R: Але якщо той народ чинитиме те, що {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} називаю злом, і не слухатиметься {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}}, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} зміню своє рішення. Я не зроблю того добра, яке обіцяв йому.

decisions.choice: I will relent concerning the good: God's promises are also bound up with the people's response
decisions.reason: As in verse 8 (meaning decision m1 there), God relents, but this time from good he had promised. A promise of blessing is no shelter for a nation that turns to evil, just as a threat of judgment is not the end for one that turns from it.

decisions.choice: not listening to my voice: not obeying
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice means to do what he says (7:23, 28; 11:4, 7).

decisions.choice: the evil in my eyes: what God judges to be evil
decisions.reason: "In my eyes" means in God's judgment, as in the formula of Judges and Kings, "did what was evil in the sight of the LORD".

decisions.choice: promised
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the good I said I would do". Balanced and Readable say "promised", which is what such a word of blessing is.

decisions.choice: hara' be'einai "わたしの目に悪であること" (L), "わたしの目に悪とされること" (B), "わたしが悪いと言うこと" (R), as 7:30; hattovah "幸い" (L, B), "良いこと" (R).
decisions.reason: JER-2 phrase (7:30).

source.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה אֱמָר־נָ֣א אֶל־אִישׁ־יְהוּדָה֩ וְעַל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י יוֹצֵ֤ר עֲלֵיכֶם֙ רָעָ֔ה וְחֹשֵׁ֥ב עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מַֽחֲשָׁבָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ נָ֗א אִ֚ישׁ מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָֽרָעָ֔ה וְהֵיטִ֥יבוּ דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם וּמַעַלְלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, say, please, to [the] man of Judah and to [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, Thus says Yahweh: Behold, I [am] forming against you evil and devising against you a plan. Turn, please, each from his way the evil, and make good your ways and your deeds.

en.L: And now, speak to {{gender:the people|the men}} of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am shaping evil against you and devising a plan against you. Turn back, each one from {{gender:their|his}} evil way, and make good your ways and your deeds.'
en.B: So now, say to {{gender:the people|the men}} of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am shaping disaster for you and making plans against you. Turn back, every one of you, from your evil way, and change your ways and your actions for the better.'
en.R: So now go and tell the people of Judah and everyone who lives in Jerusalem, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Like a potter, I am shaping disaster for you. I am making plans against you. So each of you must turn away from your evil way of life. Change the way you live and the things you do.'

es.L: Y ahora, habla, te ruego, a {{gender:la gente de Judá|los hombres de Judá}} y a los habitantes de Jerusalén, diciendo: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: He aquí, yo estoy formando un mal contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y trazando un plan contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}}, cada uno de su mal camino, y {{plural_you:mejoren sus caminos y sus obras|mejorad vuestros caminos y vuestras obras}}”.
es.B: Así que ahora, di a {{gender:la gente de Judá|los hombres de Judá}} y a los que viven en Jerusalén: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Estoy formando un desastre para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y haciendo planes contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}}, cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, de su mal camino, y {{plural_you:mejoren su manera de vivir y sus acciones|mejorad vuestra manera de vivir y vuestras acciones}}”.
es.R: Así que ahora ve y diles a la gente de Judá y a todos los que viven en Jerusalén: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Como un alfarero, estoy formando un desastre para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Estoy haciendo planes contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Así que cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:tiene|ha}} que dejar su mal camino. {{plural_you:Cambien su manera de vivir y lo que hacen|Cambiad vuestra manera de vivir y lo que hacéis}}”.

fr.L: Et maintenant, parle donc {{gender:aux gens de Juda|aux hommes de Juda}} et aux habitants de Jérusalem, en disant : “Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Voici, je façonne contre vous un mal et je forme un projet contre vous. Revenez donc, chacun de sa mauvaise voie, et rendez bonnes vos voies et vos actions.”
fr.B: Maintenant donc, dis {{gender:aux gens de Juda|aux hommes de Juda}} et aux habitants de Jérusalem : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Je façonne un malheur contre vous et je forme des projets contre vous. Revenez, chacun de vous, de votre mauvaise voie, et améliorez votre conduite et vos actions.”
fr.R: Maintenant, va dire aux gens de Juda et à tous les habitants de Jérusalem : “Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Comme un potier, je suis en train de façonner un malheur pour vous. Je fais des projets contre vous. Alors, que chacun de vous abandonne sa mauvaise conduite. Changez votre façon de vivre et ce que vous faites.”

sw.L: Basi sasa, sema na watu wa Yuda na wakazi wa Yerusalemu, ukisema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Tazama, ninawafinyangia mabaya, na kuwawazia mpango juu yenu. Rudini, kila mmoja kutoka njia yake mbaya, mkazitengeneze njia zenu na matendo yenu.'
sw.B: Basi sasa, waambie watu wa Yuda na wakazi wa Yerusalemu, 'Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Ninawafinyangia maafa na kufanya mipango dhidi yenu. Rudini, kila mmoja wenu, aache njia yake mbaya; zifanyeni njia zenu na matendo yenu kuwa mema.'
sw.R: Basi sasa nenda ukawaambie watu wa Yuda na wote wanaoishi Yerusalemu, 'Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Kama mfinyanzi, ninawafinyangia maafa. Ninafanya mipango dhidi yenu. Kwa hiyo kila mmoja wenu na aiache njia yake mbaya ya maisha. Badilisheni jinsi mnavyoishi na mambo mnayoyafanya.'

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, hãy nói với người Giu-đa và với cư dân Giê-ru-sa-lem rằng: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang nắn một điều ác nghịch cùng các ngươi và đang mưu tính một kế hoạch nghịch cùng các ngươi. Mỗi người hãy quay lại khỏi đường ác của mình, và hãy làm cho đường lối và việc làm của các ngươi nên tốt.'
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, con hãy nói với người Giu-đa và dân cư Giê-ru-sa-lem: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Ta đang nắn sẵn tai họa cho các ngươi và đang lập kế hoạch nghịch cùng các ngươi. Mỗi người trong các ngươi hãy quay lại khỏi đường ác của mình, hãy sửa đổi đường lối và việc làm của các ngươi cho tốt đẹp.'
vi.R: Vậy bây giờ con hãy đi nói với dân Giu-đa và mọi người sống tại Giê-ru-sa-lem: 'Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Như người thợ gốm, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang nắn sẵn tai họa cho các ngươi. Ta đang lập kế hoạch nghịch cùng các ngươi. Vậy mỗi người trong các ngươi phải từ bỏ lối sống gian ác của mình. Hãy thay đổi cách sống và những việc các ngươi làm.'

ko.L: 그러니 이제 유다 사람과 예루살렘 주민들에게 말하여라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 보아라, 내가 너희에게 내릴 재앙을 빚고 있고, 너희를 칠 계획을 세우고 있다. 너희는 각자 자기의 악한 길에서 돌아오너라. 너희 길과 너희 행실을 좋게 하여라.'
ko.B: 그러니 이제 유다 사람들과 예루살렘에 사는 사람들에게 말하여라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 너희에게 내릴 재앙을 빚고 있고, 너희를 칠 계획을 세우고 있다. 너희는 모두 저마다 악한 길에서 돌아오너라. 너희 길과 행실을 바르게 고쳐라.'
ko.R: 그러니 이제 가서 유다 사람들과 예루살렘에 사는 모든 사람에게 전하여라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 나는 그릇 만드는 사람처럼 너희에게 내릴 재앙을 빚고 있다. 너희를 칠 계획을 세우고 있다. 그러니 너희는 저마다 악하게 사는 길에서 돌아오너라. 너희가 사는 방식과 너희가 하는 일을 바꾸어라.'

pt.L: E agora, fala {{gender:ao povo|aos homens}} de Judá e aos habitantes de Jerusalém, dizendo: 'Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Eis que estou modelando contra vocês um mal e tramando contra vocês um plano. Voltem, cada um do seu mau caminho, e tornem bons os seus caminhos e as suas ações.'
pt.B: Agora, pois, dize {{gender:ao povo|aos homens}} de Judá e aos moradores de Jerusalém: 'Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Estou modelando uma desgraça para vocês e fazendo planos contra vocês. Voltem, cada um de vocês, do seu mau caminho, e mudem para melhor os seus caminhos e as suas ações.'
pt.R: Agora, vai e dize ao povo de Judá e a todos os que moram em Jerusalém: 'É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Como um oleiro, estou modelando uma desgraça para vocês. Estou fazendo planos contra vocês. Por isso, cada um de vocês deve abandonar o seu mau modo de viver. Mudem o jeito como vocês vivem e o que vocês fazem.'

am.L: አሁንም ለይሁዳ ሰዎችና በኢየሩሳሌም ለሚኖሩ እንዲህ ብለህ ተናገር፦ “{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል፦ እነሆ፣ በእናንተ ላይ ክፉ ነገርን እቀርጻለሁ፤ በእናንተም ላይ ዕቅድ አወጣለሁ። እያንዳንዳችሁ ከክፉ መንገዳችሁ ተመለሱ፤ መንገዳችሁንና ሥራችሁንም አሳምሩ።”
am.B: ስለዚህ አሁን ለይሁዳ ሰዎችና በኢየሩሳሌም ለሚኖሩ እንዲህ በላቸው፦ “{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል፦ በእናንተ ላይ ጥፋትን እቀርጻለሁ፤ በእናንተም ላይ ዕቅድ አወጣለሁ። እያንዳንዳችሁ ከክፉ መንገዳችሁ ተመለሱ፤ መንገዳችሁንና ሥራችሁንም አሻሽሉ።”
am.R: ስለዚህ አሁን ሂድና ለይሁዳ ሕዝብና በኢየሩሳሌም ለሚኖሩ ሁሉ እንዲህ ብለህ ንገራቸው፦ “{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል፦ ሸክላ ሠሪ እንደሚቀርጽ በእናንተ ላይ ጥፋትን እቀርጻለሁ። በእናንተ ላይ ዕቅድ አወጣለሁ። ስለዚህ እያንዳንዳችሁ ከክፉ አኗኗራችሁ ተመለሱ። አኗኗራችሁንና የምታደርጉትን ነገር ለውጡ።”

hi.L: और अब, यहूदा के {{gender:लोगों|पुरुषों}} से और यरूशलेम के निवासियों से कहो, '{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} यों कहते हैं: देखो, मैं तुम्हारे विरुद्ध बुराई गढ़ रहा हूँ और तुम्हारे विरुद्ध युक्ति सोच रहा हूँ। तुम में से हर एक अपने बुरे मार्ग से लौट आए, और अपने चालचलन और अपने काम सुधारो।'
hi.B: इसलिए अब यहूदा के {{gender:लोगों|पुरुषों}} से और यरूशलेम के रहनेवालों से कहो, '{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} यह कहते हैं: मैं तुम पर विपत्ति गढ़ रहा हूँ और तुम्हारे विरुद्ध योजना बना रहा हूँ। तुम में से हर एक अपने बुरे मार्ग से लौट आए, और अपने चालचलन और अपने कामों को सुधारो।'
hi.R: इसलिए अब जाकर यहूदा के लोगों से और यरूशलेम में रहनेवाले सब लोगों से कहो, '{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} यह कहते हैं: जैसे कुम्हार बर्तन गढ़ता है, वैसे ही मैं तुम पर विपत्ति गढ़ रहा हूँ। मैं तुम्हारे विरुद्ध योजना बना रहा हूँ। इसलिए तुम में से हर एक अपने बुरे जीवन से फिर जाए। अपना चालचलन और अपने काम बदलो।'

ru.L: И теперь скажи же {{gender:людям|мужам}} Иуды и жителям Иерусалима так: “Так говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}: Вот, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} леплю против вас зло и задумываю против вас замысел. Обратитесь же каждый от своего злого пути и исправьте ваши пути и ваши дела.”
ru.B: Итак, скажи теперь {{gender:людям|мужам}} Иуды и жителям Иерусалима: “Так говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}: Вот, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} леплю для вас бедствие и готовлю против вас замысел. Обратитесь же каждый от своего злого пути и исправьте ваши пути и ваши поступки.”
ru.R: Итак, пойди и скажи людям Иуды и всем жителям Иерусалима: “Вот что говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}: Как горшечник, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} леплю для вас бедствие. Я готовлю план против вас. Поэтому каждый из вас должен оставить свою злую жизнь. Измените то, как вы живёте, и то, что вы делаете.”

ja.L: さあ今、ユダの人々とエルサレムの住民に言いなさい。『{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。見なさい、わたしはあなたがたに対して災いを形づくり、あなたがたに対して計画を練っている。さあ、それぞれ、その悪の道から立ち帰り、あなたがたの道とあなたがたの行いを改めよ。』
ja.B: それで今、ユダの人々とエルサレムに住む者たちに言いなさい。『{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。わたしは、あなたがたに災いを形づくり、あなたがたに対して計画を立てている。だから、あなたがたはそれぞれ、悪の道から立ち帰り、自分の道と行いを改めなさい。』
ja.R: だから今、行って、ユダの人々とエルサレムに住むすべての人に言いなさい。『{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。わたしは陶工のように、あなたたちに災いを形づくっている。あなたたちに対して計画を立てている。だから、あなたたちはそれぞれ、悪い生き方をやめて、戻って来なさい。生き方を改め、することを改めなさい。』

uk.L: А тепер скажи {{gender:людям|мужам}} Юди і жителям Єрусалима, кажучи: “Так говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}: Ось {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} ліплю проти вас лихо і задумую проти вас задум. Поверніться ж, кожен зі своєї лихої дороги, і виправте ваші дороги і ваші вчинки”.
uk.B: Тож тепер скажи {{gender:людям|мужам}} Юдеї і тим, хто живе в Єрусалимі: “Так говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}: Я ліплю для вас лихо і задумую проти вас задуми. Поверніться, кожен із вас, зі своєї лихої дороги і змініть на краще свої дороги і свої дії”.
uk.R: Тож тепер іди й скажи людям Юдеї та всім, хто живе в Єрусалимі: “Ось що каже {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}: Як гончар, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} ліплю для вас лихо. Я задумую проти вас задуми. Тож кожен із вас мусить відвернутися від свого лихого життя. Змініть те, як ви живете, і те, що ви робите”.

decisions.choice: shaping: forming, the potter's own verb
decisions.reason: The word for "shaping" is the same as the word for "potter" in verses 2-6, which means "one who shapes". God speaks of himself as the potter at work on Judah: the disaster is being formed, not yet fired, and verses 7-8 have just said that it can still be turned aside.

decisions.choice: man of Judah: the people of Judah as a whole
decisions.reason: The singular noun "man" with a place name is a collective way of naming all the people of a land, as in 11:2.

decisions.choice: make good your ways and your deeds: change your conduct for the better
decisions.reason: The same call as in the temple sermon (7:3, 5) and in 26:13. "Ways" is the whole course of life, and "deeds" the things done along it.

decisions.choice: please ... now: an urging word, softening the command
decisions.reason: The little word joined to "say" and to "turn" makes the commands earnest appeals. Even while the disaster is being shaped, God pleads with the people to turn.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah, with "the men of Judah" as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew collective means the whole people, so the inclusive form is the default, as in 11:2. Readable says "the people", which needs no alternative. In Literal "each one from their evil way" has "his" as the alternative for the same reason.

decisions.choice: Like a potter
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link with the potter plain, since the shared Hebrew word (meaning decision m1) cannot be heard in English.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The message Jeremiah is to give is quoted inside the LORD's speech to him, which began in verse 6, so it takes single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: Así dice el SEÑOR: / El SEÑOR dice esto: / Esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR:
decisions.reason: The Spanish wording of "Thus says the LORD" for the whole block, followed by a colon, as in the Kings and Chronicles note.

decisions.choice: la gente de Judá, with "los hombres de Judá" as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew collective "man of Judah" means the whole people (meaning decision m2), so the inclusive form is the default, as the published Spanish has it elsewhere.

decisions.choice: ninawafinyangia
decisions.reason: Swahili "kufinyanga" (to shape clay) shares its root with "mfinyanzi" (potter), just as the Hebrew verb shares its root with "potter", so the wordplay of meaning decision m1 can be heard at every level.

decisions.choice: BWANA asema hivi: / Hivi ndivyo BWANA asemavyo: / Hili ndilo BWANA analosema:
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili wording of "Thus says the LORD" at each level (2 Kings 19:6; 1 Chronicles 17:4). "Watu wa Yuda" is already inclusive, so Swahili needs no gender alternative here.

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle le SEIGNEUR :" (L); "Le SEIGNEUR dit ceci :" (B); "Voici ce que dit le SEIGNEUR :" (R)
decisions.reason: The fixed French wording of this formula in Jeremiah 18-34, as 2 Kings 19:6 and 20:1. A message quoted inside the LORD's speech takes the inner marks “ ”.

decisions.choice: "aux gens de Juda", with "aux hommes de Juda" as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew collective "man of Judah" means the whole people, so the inclusive form is the default, as in English. "Revenez" keeps the verb "revenir" settled for shuv in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: "người Giu-đa" (the people of Judah), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người Giu-đa" and "mỗi người ... của mình" already include men and women, so the gender alternative of the English has no second wording here, as the Vietnamese style guide says.

decisions.choice: "nắn" (shape), the potter's verb
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "nắn" is what the potter does to the clay in verse 4, so the link of meaning decision m1 is heard at every level; Readable also adds "Như người thợ gốm" as the English does.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다" (L); "... 이렇게 말씀하신다" (B); "... 하시는 말씀이다" (R), with the honorific, though the formula stands inside God's words to Jeremiah
alternatives: "주가 이와 같이 말한다" (God naming himself plainly)
decisions.reason: One rule for Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezra: the messenger formula keeps the honorific even where God dictates the message, as published at 1 Kings 21:19, 2 Samuel 7:5 and 1 Chronicles 17:4; God's own words that follow stay in the plain style, without -시- for himself.

decisions.choice: "빚다" for *yotser* ("shaping")
decisions.reason: "빚다" is what a potter does with clay, so Korean keeps the link with the potter of verses 2-6 (meaning decision m1) at every level; Readable also says "그릇 만드는 사람처럼", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: modelando (every level); {{gender:ao povo|aos homens}} de Judá; cada um ... do seu caminho, with no span
decisions.reason: The verb is the potter's own (m1), and Portuguese has no verb that shares the root of "oleiro", so every level says "modelar", the verb 1:5 uses for God shaping Jeremiah, and Readable adds "Como um oleiro", as the English Readable does. The people of Judah take the setting as in 11:2; "cada um ... seu", here and in verse 12, already means anyone, so the English "their/his" has no Portuguese span.

decisions.choice: "የይሁዳ ሰዎች" (L, B), "የይሁዳ ሕዝብ" (R) without a gender span
decisions.reason: Amharic "ሰዎች" already includes men and women, so there is nothing for the gender setting to change.

decisions.choice: गढ़ना, every level
decisions.reason: The verb is the potter's own (meaning m1), and Hindi गढ़ना is the word used for the potter in verse 4, so the link can be heard at every level; Readable also adds the comparison, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: {{gender:लोगों|पुरुषों}}
decisions.reason: "The man of Judah" means the whole people, as in 17:25, so Literal and Balanced carry the English gender span; Readable says लोग with no span.

decisions.choice: леплю
decisions.reason: The verb is the potter's own (the meaning decision); "лепить" is what a potter does with clay, so the link with verses 2-6 is heard at Literal and Balanced; Readable adds "Как горшечник".

decisions.choice: yotser ra'ah "災いを形づくる" at every level, the potter's verb of 18:4 (m1; R adds "陶工のように" as the English R); shuvu "立ち帰り" (L, B), "戻って来なさい" (R); heitivu "改めよ" (L), "改めなさい" (B, R) (m3); the message in 『』.
alternatives: R "悪い生き方から離れなさい" (loses the shuv verb)
decisions.reason: JER shuv row (18:11 named there); the oracle command forms.

decisions.choice: 'ish-Yehudah "ユダの人々" and 'ish "それぞれ" carry no gender span: the Japanese is already inclusive, where the English has the people/the men and their/his (r-en-1).
decisions.reason: Style guide §7.

source.text: וְאָמְר֖וּ נוֹאָ֑שׁ כִּֽי־אַחֲרֵ֤י מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ נֵלֵ֔ךְ וְאִ֛ישׁ שְׁרִר֥וּת לִבּֽוֹ־הָרָ֖ע נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they will say, Hopeless! For after our plans we will walk, and each [the] stubbornness of his heart the evil we will do.

en.L: But they will say, 'It is hopeless! For we will walk after our own plans, and we will act, each one according to the stubbornness of {{gender:their|his}} evil heart.'"
en.B: But they will say, 'It is no use! We will follow our own plans; each of us will act in the stubbornness of our evil hearts.'"
en.R: But they will answer, 'It is no use! We will do what we have planned. Each of us will stubbornly follow our own evil heart.'"

es.L: Pero ellos dirán: “¡Es inútil! Porque iremos tras nuestros propios planes, y cada uno hará según la terquedad de su corazón malvado”».
es.B: Pero ellos dirán: “¡No sirve de nada! Seguiremos nuestros propios planes; cada uno de nosotros actuará según la terquedad de su corazón malvado”».
es.R: Pero ellos responderán: “¡No sirve de nada! Haremos lo que hemos planeado. Cada uno de nosotros seguirá tercamente lo que le dicte su corazón malvado”».

fr.L: Mais ils diront : “C’est sans espoir ! Car nous marcherons selon nos projets, et nous agirons chacun selon l’obstination de son cœur mauvais.” »
fr.B: Mais ils diront : “Inutile ! Nous suivrons nos propres projets ; chacun de nous agira selon l’obstination de son cœur mauvais.” »
fr.R: Mais ils répondront : “Ça ne sert à rien ! Nous ferons ce que nous avons décidé. Chacun de nous suivra avec obstination les désirs mauvais de son cœur.” »

sw.L: Lakini watasema, 'Hakuna tumaini! Kwa maana tutafuata mipango yetu wenyewe, na kila mmoja atatenda kwa ukaidi wa moyo wake mbaya.'"
sw.B: Lakini watasema, 'Haifai kitu! Tutafuata mipango yetu wenyewe; kila mmoja wetu atatenda kwa ukaidi wa moyo wake mbaya.'"
sw.R: Lakini watajibu, 'Haifai kitu! Tutafanya yale tuliyopanga. Kila mmoja wetu atafuata kwa ukaidi moyo wake mbaya.'"

vi.L: Nhưng chúng sẽ nói: 'Vô vọng rồi! Vì chúng tôi sẽ đi theo các mưu kế của mình, và mỗi người chúng tôi sẽ làm theo sự cứng cỏi của lòng gian ác mình.'"
vi.B: Nhưng chúng sẽ nói: 'Vô ích thôi! Chúng tôi sẽ theo kế hoạch riêng của mình; mỗi người chúng tôi sẽ cứ đi theo sự cứng cỏi của lòng gian ác mình.'"
vi.R: Nhưng chúng sẽ trả lời: 'Vô ích thôi! Chúng tôi sẽ làm theo điều chúng tôi đã định. Mỗi người chúng tôi sẽ cứ cứng đầu làm theo lòng gian ác của mình.'"

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 말할 것이다. '소용없다! 우리는 우리의 계획을 따라 걷고, 각자 자기의 악한 마음의 고집대로 행할 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 이렇게 말할 것이다. '소용없다! 우리는 우리 계획대로 하겠다. 우리는 저마다 악한 마음의 고집대로 하겠다.'"
ko.R: 그러나 그들은 이렇게 대답할 것이다. '소용없다! 우리는 우리가 계획한 대로 하겠다. 우리는 저마다 고집스럽게 우리의 악한 마음을 따르겠다.'"

pt.L: Mas eles dirão: 'É inútil! Pois andaremos segundo os nossos próprios planos, e agiremos, cada um, segundo a obstinação do seu coração mau.'"
pt.B: Mas eles dirão: 'Não adianta! Vamos seguir os nossos próprios planos; cada um de nós vai agir segundo a teimosia do seu coração mau.'"
pt.R: Mas eles vão responder: 'Não adianta! Vamos fazer o que planejamos. Cada um de nós vai seguir teimosamente o seu próprio coração mau.'"

am.L: እነርሱ ግን፦ “ተስፋ የለውም! የራሳችንን ዕቅድ ተከትለን እንሄዳለንና፤ እያንዳንዳችንም እንደ ክፉ ልባችን እልከኝነት እናደርጋለን” ይላሉ።»
am.B: እነርሱ ግን፦ “ምንም ዋጋ የለውም! የራሳችንን ዕቅድ እንከተላለን፤ እያንዳንዳችንም በክፉ ልባችን እልከኝነት እንሄዳለን” ይላሉ።»
am.R: እነርሱ ግን፦ “ምንም ፋይዳ የለውም! ያቀድነውን እናደርጋለን። እያንዳንዳችን በእልከኝነት ክፉ ልባችንን እንከተላለን” ብለው ይመልሳሉ።»

hi.L: पर वे कहेंगे, 'कोई आशा नहीं! क्योंकि हम अपनी ही युक्तियों के पीछे चलेंगे, और हम हर एक अपने बुरे मन के हठ के अनुसार करेंगे।'"
hi.B: पर वे कहेंगे, 'कोई लाभ नहीं! हम अपनी ही योजनाओं पर चलेंगे; हम में से हर एक अपने बुरे मन के हठ के अनुसार करेगा।'"
hi.R: पर वे जवाब देंगे, 'कोई फ़ायदा नहीं! हमने जो सोचा है, वही करेंगे। हम में से हर एक हठ करके अपने बुरे मन के पीछे चलेगा।'"

ru.L: Но они скажут: “Безнадёжно! Потому что мы пойдём за нашими замыслами и будем поступать каждый по упрямству своего злого сердца.”»
ru.B: Но они скажут: “Бесполезно! Мы будем следовать своим замыслам, каждый из нас будет поступать по упрямству своего злого сердца.”»
ru.R: Но они ответят: “Бесполезно! Мы будем делать то, что задумали. Каждый из нас будет упрямо следовать своему злому сердцу.”»

ja.L: しかし、彼らは言う。『もう望みはない！わたしたちは自分たちの計画に従って歩み、それぞれ自分の悪い心のかたくなさのままに行う。』」
ja.B: しかし、彼らは言う。『むだだ！わたしたちは自分たちの計画に従う。わたしたちはそれぞれ、悪いかたくなな心のままに行う。』」
ja.R: しかし、彼らはこう答える。『むだだ！わたしたちは自分たちが計画したとおりにする。わたしたちはそれぞれ、自分の悪い心にかたくなに従う。』」

uk.L: Але вони скажуть: “Марно! Бо ми ходитимемо за своїми задумами, і чинитимемо, кожен, за впертістю свого злого серця”».
uk.B: Але вони скажуть: “Даремно! Ми йтимемо за своїми задумами; кожен із нас чинитиме за впертістю свого злого серця”».
uk.R: Але вони відповідатимуть: “Даремно! Ми робитимемо те, що задумали. Кожен із нас уперто йтиме за своїм злим серцем”».

decisions.choice: hopeless: it is no use, we have given up
decisions.reason: The word means that something is past hope. The people do not mean that they cannot turn but that they will not: there is no point in asking them (as in 2:25). It is despair turned into defiance.

decisions.choice: they will say: God tells Jeremiah in advance how the people will answer
decisions.reason: The verb looks ahead. Before Jeremiah has spoken, God knows the reply, and the oracle of verses 13-17 answers it.

decisions.choice: our plans ... the stubbornness of his evil heart: they will follow their own designs, not God's
decisions.reason: "Plans" is the word God used for his own plan in verse 11, so the people set their plans against his. "The stubbornness of the heart" is Jeremiah's phrase for a will set hard against God (7:24; 11:8; 13:10); the heart is the seat of thought and will.

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of his evil heart / ... of our evil hearts / stubbornly follow our own evil heart
decisions.reason: The wording settled for this phrase in Jeremiah, turned into the first person because the people speak of themselves. The gender setting in Literal gives "his" as the alternative for "each one ... their".

decisions.choice: closing quotation marks
decisions.reason: The people's reply ends the message Jeremiah is to give and the LORD's speech that began in verse 6.

decisions.choice: la terquedad de su corazón malvado (Literal, Balanced); seguirá tercamente (Readable)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's phrase for a will set hard against God keeps one Spanish wording through the block, as the English keeps "stubbornness".

decisions.choice: ukaidi wa moyo wake mbaya / kwa ukaidi
decisions.reason: "Ukaidi" (stubborn defiance) is used for Jeremiah's phrase throughout this block; "ugumu wa moyo" suggests hardness rather than wilful refusal.

decisions.choice: "l'obstination de son cœur mauvais" (L, B); "suivra avec obstination les désirs mauvais de son cœur" (R)
decisions.reason: The French wording settled for sherirut lev in Jeremiah 18-34. "Chacun ... son" is already generic in French, so no gender setting is needed where the English Literal has one.

decisions.choice: "sự cứng cỏi của lòng gian ác mình" / "lòng gian ác cứng cỏi" / "cứ cứng lòng làm theo ý gian ác"
decisions.reason: One wording at each level for Jeremiah's "stubbornness of the heart" (sherirut lev), used through these chapters; here in the people's own mouth ("chúng tôi").

decisions.choice: "악한 마음의 고집대로" (L, B); "고집스럽게 ... 악한 마음을 따르다" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *sherirut lev* in Jeremiah, turned into the first person because the people speak of themselves. "완악하다" is an older church word that young readers seldom know.

decisions.choice: no'ash "もう望みはない" (L), "むだだ" (B, R) (m1); sherirut libbo hara' as 16:12; the people's answer plain, in 『』 inside God's words, both closed here.
decisions.reason: JEREMIAH CONVENTIONS (sherirut lev).
